subject: Bluecrest production latency & error surge — immediate RCA and owners
messages:
From: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@bluecrest.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: elena@bluecrest.com, sre@bluecrest.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: checkout latency spike + errors (us-west)

Irene —

We started seeing a severe degradation in checkout experience at ~08:45 PDT: p50/generation latency jumped from ~120ms to ~900ms, p95 above 3.2s, and our 5m error rate climbed to ~8%. Throughput for the feature dropped ~40% relative to baseline which is causing visible failures in our checkout flow.

Attached is a quick perf snapshot from our synthetic tests (perf-snapshot-20270622.csv). We’re currently routing 60% of traffic to Redwood’s hosted route. We need an immediate triage, an indication of whether this is a config/deployment issue or something on the inference runtime, and an ETA for mitigation. Our business team is on calls — this is impacting a live campaign.

Please escalate to engineering and let us know next steps.

– Tom Hargreaves
Head of Platform, Bluecrest Commerce
Tom.H@bluecrest.com

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: tom.h@bluecrest.com, elena@bluecrest.com, sre@bluecrest.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Production: checkout latency spike + errors (us-west) — initial RCA draft

Team — quick engineering summary (short form; full notes in linked draft):

What happened (summary):
- Timeline: a runtime scheduling change (continuous-batching heuristic v2.1.4) was deployed at 08:30 PDT 22 Jun to reduce tail latency for high-concurrency workloads. After deployment, we observed increased batch size coalescing under a specific token-length distribution Bluecrest uses. The heuristic over-aggregated batches for short-lived sessions which caused memory pressure and intermittent CPU stalls on the host kernel path.
- Observable symptoms: elevated p50/p95 token latency, increased queue wait times, and a secondary effect where some requests timed out and surfaced as an 5xx error (volume ~8%). Throughput drop was primarily due to longer per-request processing and backpressure into the request queue.

Root cause: an interaction between the new batching heuristic and Bluecrest’s usage pattern (high short-sequence fan-out). The heuristic incorrectly prioritized large batch formation in the presence of many concurrent connections, causing inefficient GPU kernel dispatch and occasional memory thrash.

Immediate mitigations completed (24 Jun):
- Rolled back batching heuristic to v2.1.3 at 11:10 PDT on 22 Jun (rollback confirmed successful).
- Applied a temporary runtime throttle to cap batch size for affected tenant routes (soft cap = 32 tokens).
- Burst Dedicated capacity to reduce queueing while fix is validated.

Permanent corrective work planned (owners & ETA):
- Hotfix: patch batching heuristic to include per-tenant sequence-profile guardrails — owner: k.iyer@redwood.com — ETA: 2027-06-26 EOD.
- Load-profile testing: new synthetic workload that mirrors Bluecrest traffic to be added to pre-deploy canary — owner: eng-test team (assigned in BLU-4321) — ETA: 2027-07-02.
- Instrumentation: add per-tenant batch/kv-cache telemetry to detect re-emergence — owner: observability team — ETA: 2027-07-09.

Documents and artifacts: rca-draft-20270624.md (drive link), Jira BLU-4321 contains the post-incident tasks.

Notes: rollback removed the pathological behavior but we want to push a hotfix before re-enabling the heuristic. Will coordinate with Bluecrest for a staged re-enable window.

-Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Bluecrest commitments & owner register — verification steps and closure criteria

Tom / Elena —

Thanks for working through this with us. Below is the concise commitment register and owners. We’ll treat this as the single source for closure items.

Commitments (high-level):
1) Hotfix batching heuristic with per-tenant guardrails — owner: Karthik Iyer (karthik.iyer@redwood.com) — due: 2027-06-26 EOD.
2) Canary plan to re-enable heuristic in low-traffic window; joint test with Bluecrest — owner: Irene Choi (irene.choi@redwood.com) — due: 2027-07-05 (canary window).
3) Add per-tenant batch telemetry and alerting — owner: Observability team (ticket BLU-4321) — due: 2027-07-09.
4) Post-fix load validation using Bluecrest synthetic workload — owner: Eng Test (linked in BLU-4321) — due: 2027-07-02.
5) Business-level SLA review and credit evaluation if repeat issue — owner: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.com) — due: 2027-07-10.

Verification and closure criteria:
- Hotfix deployed and validated across canary then staged rollout without latency regressions.
- Telemetry shows stable batch sizes and no elevated queue wait times for 72 hours post-rollout.
- Bluecrest signs off on canary results.

Attachments: commitments-bluecrest-20270625.pdf (commitment register), rca-draft-20270624.md (engineering notes).

Next steps: Irene will confirm the canary schedule with Bluecrest and loop in product ops for a staged re-enable. Karthik will ping when the hotfix is available for canary. Marissa will coordinate any commercial follow-ups and track SLA remediation conversations.

Please reply with any edits to the owner/due list — we’ll keep this thread as the single timeline.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
